topic:
Ordinary new-topic generation after the mandated revival_remaining.sh count printed zero. This is not a revival of the rejected known-generator commutator: the target is a sharp partially identified continuous-time component risk when only grouped factual event laws are observed. Retain the exact active-ceiling finite-piece theorem over every compatible measurable hazard model; inactive-ceiling pulse bounds, interval existence, mesh rates and generic confidence inversion cannot substitute for it. MODEL: Fixed known T>0,L>0, arbitrary finite fixed grid 0=t0<...<tK=T. iid subjects, A randomized Bernoulli(1/2), no covariates or additional censoring. Absorbing first-event system: four deterministic Lebesgue-measurable cause-specific hazards lambda_j^a:[0,T]->[0,L], a in {0,1}, j in {1,2}. Under component intervention (aY,aD), cause1 hazard is lambda1^aY and cause2 hazard lambda2^aD; survival is exp(-integral(lambda1^aY+lambda2^aD)). This hazard-splicing restriction defines the causal model; no latent independence beyond what realizes these intervention laws is asserted. All such quadruples are allowed. Observe only A and first-failure inspection bin plus adjudicated cause, or survival to T; retain neither exact failure time nor within-bin order. The population observation is factual conditional bin triples z_ak=(p_ak,q_ak,s_ak), summing to1. Survival is positive because hazards are bounded. Restrict z to compatible observations. Target psi=integral_0^T exp(-Lambda1^1(t)-Lambda2^0(t)) lambda1^1(t)dt, and SDE=psi-observed arm0 cause1 risk. No sensitivity analysis: the hazard-component model is maintained and coarsening produces partial identification. KERNEL: Conjecture over every L,T,K,grid and compatible z: derive a sharp constructive representation of the full attainable hybrid incidence-survival frontier for ONE bin, sufficient to evaluate its support envelope H_z(v)=sup(r+v*s) and lower envelope h_z(v)=inf(r+v*s), for v in [0,1]. Here (r,s) is the hybrid cause1 incidence and end-survival within that bin, generated by four bounded hazards reproducing both factual triples. These suprema define the object, NOT the promised solution. The hard assertion is that exact envelopes admit a uniformly finite switching representation: there exists a universal finite integer B, independent of z,L,bin width, such that each envelope value is attained by compatible piecewise-constant hazard quadruples with at most B common subintervals; levels may be anywhere in [0,L], not necessarily bang-bang. Derive an explicit valid B and finite parameter optimization with endpoint probability constraints and objective expressed in elementary exponential integrals; characterize the optimizing incidence-survival tradeoff beyond merely invoking general optimal control. Prove global endpoints by backward evaluation U_(K+1)=D_(K+1)=0, U_k=H_zk(U_(k+1)), D_k=h_zk(D_(k+1)), including compatible full-model gluing. Also derive the worst-case identification-width order over compatible z: for each fixed M>0 and LT<=M, sufficiently small L*max(bin width), sup_z(U1-D1) is bounded above and below by positive constants depending only on M times L^2*sum(bin width^2). Constants and the finite-switch bound B are delegated derivation objects; the finite-switch EXISTENCE and matched mesh order are conjectures, not established claims. Sampling rung: invert an explicit simultaneous multinomial confidence region through the endpoint computation to obtain an interval containing the entire population identified set with coverage at least1-alpha uniformly over the class; report computational approximation error separately if used. No one-bin result or generic discretization substitutes for the hard finite-switch frontier theorem. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: The presolve derives exact factual-bin compatibility, compactness and interval sharpness in survival-flow coordinates, an exact active-ceiling frontier with one saturated factual arm, and compatible global gluing. For two positive factual triples with survival exp(-1.6), an exact five-piece family has a quartic restricted support optimizer: at continuation zero its hybrid risk is 0.47070698750422113 with survival 0.18947781529999005. Root independently checked the path probabilities; global optimality is not established. Switching equations make two nuisance controls monotone; a proposed simultaneous logistic singular obstruction fails the Goh necessary condition, while single-control singular arcs admit exact pulse replacement. Matched mesh-width bounds and multinomial inversion coverage are derived supporting results. Fixed-grid optimizations supply feasible values only, and current primary checks found no direct solved collision.
UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Prove parameter-uniform endpoint-preserving compression of optimal alternating bang trajectories when both nuisance hazards are saturated and factual-incidence multipliers are negative; assemble all flat, singular, abnormal and boundary cases into an explicit universal finite B.
EARLY KILL TEST: Parameterize two full four-corner cycles, compute factual constraints and support objective exactly, and examine the constrained Hessian for an improving cycle-deletion direction or an optimality-certified obstruction. Do not replace the finite-piece theorem with mesh bounds or numerical gridding.

open_problems.open_problem: Determine whether every one-bin support extremum of the hybrid incidence-survival pair under two bounded measurable factual hazard pairs is attained by a common piecewise-constant hazard quadruple with a universal number B of pieces, or whether compatible data can force unbounded switching.

source_refs.claim: Separable effects are identified under treatment decomposition, but partial identification from lost within-bin timing is not addressed.
source_refs.author: Mats J. Stensrud, Jessica G. Young, Vanessa Didelez, James M. Robins, Miguel A. Hernán

source_refs.claim: The continuous-time separable risk is identified when cause-specific hazards are recoverable; fixed grouped failure bins are not treated.
source_refs.author: Torben Martinussen, Mats Julius Stensrud

source_refs.claim: Discretely measured competing risks yield nonlinear sharp-bound programs, but no bounded-hazard component-intervention frontier is derived.
source_refs.author: Dongwoo Kim

source_refs.claim: Smooth bounded-control problems can possess optimal chattering arcs at singular junctions, so Pontryagin conditions alone do not imply finite switching.

open_problems.why_unsolved: The prior proposal points toward finite-moment compression, while the web literature separates into exact-history identification of separable effects, discrete competing-risk bounds, and generic optimal-control relaxations. None preserves simultaneously the factual incidence constraints, hybrid objective, endpoint survival, and chronological ordering of exponentiated cumulative hazards. Unordered moment atomicity loses that ordering, and known singular-junction examples permit chattering. The missing step is therefore parameter-uniform endpoint-preserving compression across alternating saturated nuisance controls, negative incidence multipliers, singular arcs, abnormal extremals, and boundary regimes.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An explicit universal integer B and an equivalent finite optimization over at most B common subintervals with elementary exponential-integral constraints, accompanied by a complete global-optimality proof, or a compatible-data family proving that no universal B exists.

writing_exemplar.why: Its motivation moves from the interpretive failure of ordinary competing-risk contrasts to component interventions and then to identification.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Competing events obscure pathway-specific causal meaning -> treatment is decomposed into event-specific components -> resolved histories identify hybrid risks -> grouped histories leave a sharp hazard-splicing frontier requiring finite structural characterization

method_exemplars.technique: Encode discrete competing-risk restrictions as nonlinear equalities and inequalities and eliminate them sequentially; adapt the proof to survival-flow endpoint constraints.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the closest econometric sharp-bounds construction for discretely measured competing risks, although the new target is a cross-arm component risk over bounded hazards.

method_exemplars.technique: Lift nonlinear trajectories to occupation measures, derive moment relaxations and dual value certificates, and isolate conditions for equality with the ordinary-control problem.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The one-bin frontier is a bounded nonlinear control problem with integral endpoint constraints; the unresolved addition is exact recovery by a uniformly finite ordinary control.

method_exemplars.technique: Use the continuous-time hazard representation and influence-function construction for separable incidence as the resolved-time estimation benchmark.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It concerns the same causal risk and identifies precisely which regularity is lost when grouped data turn the target into optimized endpoints.

open_problems.open_problem: Establish the sharp worst-compatible inspection-mesh law for hazard-spliced component risk: whether, uniformly for LT bounded, the maximal identification width is of order L² times the sum of squared bin widths.

source_refs.claim: The generalized separable-effects theory imposes a within-interval temporal order and only argues qualitatively that its importance vanishes on fine grids.
source_refs.author: Mats J. Stensrud, Miguel A. Hernán, Eric J. Tchetgen Tchetgen, James M. Robins, Vanessa Didelez, Jessica G. Young

source_refs.claim: The review reports little guidance on when continuous-time approximations to grouped competing-risk data are adequate.
source_refs.author: Matthias Schmid, Moritz Berger

source_refs.claim: Current-status competing-risk estimators have cube-root statistical rates, which do not characterize deterministic causal identification loss as the mesh shrinks.
source_refs.author: Piet Groeneboom, Marloes H. Maathuis, Jon A. Wellner

source_refs.claim: Grouped competing-risk inference is developed for factual cumulative-incidence functions, but no causal component-risk identification modulus is given.
source_refs.author: Marloes H. Maathuis, Michael G. Hudgens

open_problems.why_unsolved: Existing rate results concern sampling error for factual subdistribution functions, whereas the desired quantity is an adversarial identification modulus over all compatible bounded measurable hazard quadruples. The missing upper-bound step is a uniform second-order cancellation showing why arbitrary within-bin rearrangement contributes only order L²Δ_k² after survival propagation. The matching lower bound additionally requires compatible factual triples and hazard rearrangements whose local losses accumulate under the exact backward support recursion rather than cancel after global gluing.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A two-sided bound c_M L²Σ_kΔ_k² ≤ sup_z[U_1(z)−D_1(z)] ≤ C_M L²Σ_kΔ_k² for sufficiently small L max_kΔ_k, with positive constants depending only on M and explicit compatible hazard/data witnesses for the lower order.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames the practical unresolved choice between intrinsically grouped-time analysis and continuous-time approximation.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Event times are commonly grouped -> continuous-time approximations are routinely substituted -> the literature lacks a criterion for harmless grouping -> a sharp causal identification modulus supplies that criterion

method_exemplars.technique: Start from the exact continuous-time product-integral formula and expand controlled perturbations of the two cause-specific cumulative hazards.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Grouped observations replace the formula's known hazard inputs by within-bin equivalence classes, making its second-order cross-hazard term the natural source of the mesh modulus.

method_exemplars.technique: Exploit the multinomial structure of grouped competing-risk probabilities to derive confidence intervals under the actual observation law.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies limit theory for the factual grouped probabilities feeding the causal endpoint map and separates sampling scale from deterministic mesh-width loss.

open_problems.open_problem: Characterize the Hadamard directional derivative of the recursively composed sharp endpoint map from grouped factual multinomial probabilities to the component-risk interval at optimizer ties, compatibility boundaries, and active-ceiling transitions.

source_refs.excerpt: Fang--Santos Theorem 2.1 conclusion exactly gives ... under ... directional-differentiability

source_refs.claim: Directionally differentiable transformations admit delta-method limits, while the ordinary bootstrap generally fails without full differentiability.
source_refs.author: Zheng Fang, Andres Santos

source_refs.claim: Marginal optimization creates directionally differentiable value-function statistics requiring derivative-aware resampling, but moving feasible sets from compatibility constraints are not covered.
source_refs.author: Sergio Firpo, Antonio F. Galvao, Thomas Parker

open_problems.why_unsolved: The cited delta method applies only after directional differentiability is proved. Here every one-bin endpoint is a nonconvex value function whose feasible set itself changes with the factual triples, and backward composition propagates kinks from multiple switching-pattern optimizers, active hazard ceilings, and compatibility-boundary constraints. Standard Danskin arguments handle a fixed feasible set and therefore do not directly produce the required derivative or control its composition across bins.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A tangential Hadamard directional-differentiability theorem for z↦(D_1(z),U_1(z)), with the derivative expressed as an auxiliary optimization over active primal-dual solutions and a consistent numerical-delta or multiplier limit law for the estimated endpoints.

writing_exemplar.why: It motivates inference by first isolating the nonsmooth value-function operation and then deriving a derivative-aware procedure.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Sharp bounds are optimization value functions -> optimizer changes destroy ordinary differentiability -> conventional bootstrap inference becomes unreliable -> derive the moving-feasible-set derivative of the grouped-hazard endpoint recursion

method_exemplars.technique: Apply the directional delta method, diagnose ordinary-bootstrap inconsistency, and estimate the directional derivative for resampling.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Once the endpoint derivative is established, the empirical grouped law has a finite-dimensional Gaussian limit to which this machinery applies.

method_exemplars.technique: Represent derivatives of marginally optimized value functions through active optimizers and combine them with derivative-aware bootstrap draws.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired lower and upper endpoints are recursively composed optimization values, with the additional complication of probability-dependent feasible sets.

open_problems.open_problem: For a bounded-intensity continuous-time illness-death model observed only through grouped state-transition histories, characterize the sharp identified set of a separable terminal-event risk and determine whether one-bin support extrema admit a switching bound depending only on the transition graph.

source_refs.claim: Continuous-time illness-death separable effects are point identified and estimated under resolved transition data.
source_refs.author: Marie Skov Breum, Anders Munch, Thomas A. Gerds, Torben Martinussen

source_refs.claim: Coarsened progressive multi-state histories are handled through parametric likelihood methods rather than sharp nonparametric bounds.
source_refs.author: Marcus Westerberg

source_refs.claim: Sequential nonlinear programs yield bounds for discretely measured competing risks but do not cover transient-state flow or separable multi-state interventions.
source_refs.author: Dongwoo Kim

open_problems.why_unsolved: Searches combining separable effects with grouped or interval-censored multi-state histories found resolved-time point-identification papers and parametric coarsened-data likelihoods, but no sharp bounded-intensity frontier. The first proof step that changes is the state-flow representation: the absorbing two-cause system has one at-risk mass, whereas the illness-death graph has multiple transient masses and terminal incidence arriving through distinct ordered paths. Its one-bin feasible object is therefore higher-dimensional, and neither two-risk sequential inequalities nor resolved-time influence functions establish sharpness or finite switching after grouping.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An explicit finite-dimensional support-function recursion for the grouped-data identified set of the separable terminal risk, with constructive full-model gluing and either a transition-graph-dependent switching bound or a compatible chattering counterexample.

writing_exemplar.why: It formulates the destination estimand through an illness-death target trial and explains why component interventions avoid undefined-mediator problems.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: A terminal event truncates an intermediate event -> ordinary mediation interventions become ill-defined -> component interventions define separable illness-death effects -> grouped transition histories replace point identification by a sharp multi-state frontier

method_exemplars.technique: Translate grouped event observations into nonlinear probability constraints and eliminate bins sequentially.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The destination again has discretely observed competing event paths, but the constraint system must be lifted from two durations to coupled transient-state flows.

method_exemplars.technique: Represent controlled multi-state flows by occupation measures and obtain global moment-dual bounds before attempting finite-switch recovery.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Occupation-measure certificates provide a graph-agnostic benchmark for the higher-dimensional support problem.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt the resolved-data influence-function derivation to regular sharp endpoints after establishing directional differentiability.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies estimator construction and limit theory for the same destination causal risk before grouping.

open_problems.open_problem: Construct a computationally certified interval containing the entire sharp hazard-spliced identified set with at least 1−α coverage uniformly over compatible two-arm grouped multinomial laws, including sparse boundary cells and nearly point-identified cases.

source_refs.claim: Naive confidence intervals for partially identified parameters can lose uniform validity as identification width changes.
source_refs.author: Guido W. Imbens, Charles F. Manski

source_refs.claim: Likelihood-level-set inversion gives nonasymptotic multinomial confidence regions with controlled coverage for any finite category count.
source_refs.author: Djalil Chafaï, Didier Concordet
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

source_refs.claim: Exact minimum-average-volume confidence regions can be constructed for multinomial probability vectors, but their images under optimized causal set maps are not considered.
source_refs.author: Matthew L. Malloy, Ardhendu Tripathy, Robert D. Nowak

source_refs.claim: Exact inference is available for functions of parameters from multiple multinomial samples, but not for a set-valued nonconvex endpoint optimization.
source_refs.author: Michael C. Sachs, Erin E. Gabriel, Michael P. Fay

open_problems.why_unsolved: Exact multinomial input-law regions already exist, so the unresolved work is not generic confidence inversion. The endpoint map is defined only on the compatibility region and requires two nonconvex global optimizations whose active switching patterns change at boundaries. A valid implementation must prove that projection through the exact endpoint recursion covers both population endpoints, handle empty empirical compatibility intersections, and convert optimization residuals or relaxations into outward one-sided error bounds rather than reporting gridded feasible values as exact extrema.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An explicit inversion algorithm and finite-sample or uniform-asymptotic result proving P_z([D_1(z),U_1(z)]⊆CI_n)≥1−α for every compatible z, together with deterministic outward enlargement rules that separately certify numerical lower- and upper-endpoint errors.

writing_exemplar.why: It distinguishes coverage of a true parameter from coverage of an entire identification region and foregrounds nonuniformity as the region narrows.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: The population target is an interval -> endpoint estimation creates competing coverage objectives -> collapsing widths make naive inference nonuniform -> invert grouped multinomial laws while certifying the nonconvex endpoint computation

method_exemplars.technique: Invert likelihood covering collections to obtain controlled-coverage regions on each multinomial simplex before mapping them through the endpoint program.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Each randomized arm produces exactly the finite multinomial law required as the input confidence object.

method_exemplars.technique: Use likelihood ordering to construct exact small-volume regions for multinomial parameters.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A tight input region directly controls conservatism after projection, especially with sparse cause-by-bin cells.

literature_map:
Stensrud, Young, Didelez, Robins, and Hernán (JASA 2022; arXiv:1901.09472) define separable effects through treatment decomposition and dismissible-component restrictions.
Stensrud et al. (Lifetime Data Analysis 2021; arXiv:2004.14824) generalize identification to time-varying structures but retain within-interval temporal ordering and give only a qualitative fine-grid argument.
Martinussen and Stensrud (Biometrics 2023; arXiv:2008.13126) give continuous-time hazard formulas, influence functions, and robust estimators under resolved event times.
Honoré and Lleras-Muney (Econometrica 2006; DOI 10.1111/j.1468-0262.2006.00722.x) establish foundational bounds for competing-risk models with interval data without independence of latent risks.
Kim (Journal of Econometrics 2023; DOI 10.1016/j.jeconom.2021.07.007) turns discretely measured competing-risk partial identification into sequential nonlinear constraint solving with bootstrap inference.
Groeneboom, Maathuis, and Wellner (Annals of Statistics 2008; arXiv:math/0609020 and math/0609021) establish cube-root rates and non-Gaussian limits for factual current-status competing-risk subdistributions.
Maathuis and Hudgens (Biometrika 2011; arXiv:0909.4856) treat continuous, discrete, and grouped inspection times and construct confidence intervals for factual cumulative incidences.
Schmid and Berger (WIREs Computational Statistics 2021; DOI 10.1002/wics.1529) emphasize the lack of guidance on when continuous-time approximations to grouped competing-risk data are adequate.
No located paper combines fixed grouped factual bin triples, bounded measurable continuous-time hazards, and cross-arm hazard splicing into a sharp component-risk frontier.
Lasserre, Henrion, Prieur, and Trélat (SIAM JCO 2008; arXiv:math/0703377) provide occupation-measure global bounds, but convergence does not imply exact finite switching.
Zhu, Trélat, and Cerf (DCDS-B 2016; DOI 10.3934/dcdsb.2016.21.1347) prove optimal chattering at singular junctions, showing why a universal switching bound requires special structure.
Bayer and Teichmann (Proceedings AMS 2006; arXiv:math/0502473) give finite atomic representations for finitely many moments, but unordered atoms do not preserve nonlinear chronological survival dynamics.
Fang and Santos (Review of Economic Studies 2019; arXiv:1404.3763) and Firpo, Galvao, and Parker (Journal of Econometrics 2023; arXiv:1911.10215) provide derivative-aware inference for nonsmooth transforms and value functions.
Chafaï and Concordet (JASA 2009; arXiv:0805.1971), Malloy, Tripathy, and Nowak (arXiv:2002.01044), and Sachs, Gabriel, and Fay (arXiv:2406.19141) provide exact multinomial-region or functional-inversion machinery.
Breum et al. (Lifetime Data Analysis 2023; DOI 10.1007/s10985-023-09601-y) and Westerberg (Statistical Methods in Medical Research 2023; DOI 10.1177/09622802231155010) expose the adjacent unresolved combination of separable illness-death effects and grouped transition histories.
